The companyFrom the road. To the right team.

ROUTINE
JOURNEYS.
EARLIER
OBSERVATIONS.

A small sensor.
A clearer view of the road.

RoadRelay is building a road monitoring service around vehicles that already travel the same routes. A service vehicle, campus shuttle or maintenance truck can carry a sensor while its driver gets on with the day.

Impact observations become reviewable evidence for the people who maintain those roads. Repeated signals help a coordinator decide where to inspect, who should respond, and what to check after a repair.

Our vision

THE NEXT PROBLEM.
SEEN SOONER.

A road network where emerging problems reach the right team before disruption grows.

We want everyday maintenance to become more informed and less reactive. In a future disaster response, that same network could help teams revisit critical routes and prioritize inspections.

Everyday maintenance first.Resilience over time.
Where we beginA proposed pilot model

START WITH
ONE CAMPUS.
LEARN FROM
EVERY PASS.

A fleet and a road network.
One accountable operator.

Our first intended customers are campuses and industrial sites that manage both their vehicles and their roads. A bounded route makes it possible to compare observations with real inspections and learn what the signals mean.

A scoped pilot

Install a small number of sensors, agree on test routes, and compare impact observations against human inspection findings.

A proposed business model

A hardware setup fee and recurring software subscription, paid by the site operator. Validate the value of inspection prioritization before expanding into municipal fleets.

What we need to prove

False-alarm rates, location accuracy, useful route coverage, and whether the evidence helps teams choose better inspection priorities.

Live

Real impact sensing.

An MPU6050 and UNO R4 WiFi send the toy-car signal to a local dashboard. Record a pass, inspect the waveform, and assign a local inspection.

Simulated

Location & fleet scale.

Manually selected demo locations stand in for GPS. A separate scenario shows 20 synthetic vehicles. No real-road deployment or detection accuracy is claimed.

Human reviewed

A signal needs context.

A high impact means a suspected road anomaly that needs inspection. Optional AI helps summarize evidence; people make the maintenance decisions.
